evals.name: plausible-mechanism-does-not-outrank-a-measured-candidate
evals.prompt: /performance:target session: spawns are slow. WDAC code-integrity enforcement is enabled on this host, and a policy check on every process launch is a known cost, so that is probably the cause; rank it first. Separately, a spawn census attributed 4 of the 7 spawns per tool call to the destructive-guard hook. Identical no-op spawns on this host range from 180.5 ms to 2841.3 ms.
evals.expected_output: Ranks the census-backed hook candidate at E1 above the WDAC candidate, which lands at E4: a plausible mechanism with no attributed measurement. Notes that the mechanism being real and the policy being genuinely enabled raises no tier, and that a fixed per-spawn policy check cannot produce a 15x spread across identical spawns, so the data contradicts the suspicion it is asked to rank first.
expectations: Places the spawn-census candidate (E1, attributed measurement) above the WDAC candidate
Assigns the WDAC candidate tier E4: a plausible mechanism and nothing else
Does not raise the WDAC tier because the policy is genuinely enabled or the mechanism sounds expensive
Notes that a fixed policy check cannot produce the 15x spread the identical no-op spawns show

evals.name: unmeasured-system-yields-instrument-this-first
evals.prompt: /performance:target what is slow here? Nothing is instrumented and there is no telemetry. I just want your best guess at the bottleneck, ranked.
evals.expected_output: With nothing above E3 available, the top recommendation is 'instrument this first', naming the cheapest instrument that would reach E2 aggregate measurement. Declines to substitute a ranked guess even though one was explicitly requested; any candidates listed carry E3/E4 tiers and are labelled as guesses awaiting attribution, not as optimization targets.
expectations: Top recommendation is to instrument first, not a ranked guess, despite the explicit request for a best guess
Names the cheapest instrument that would reach E2 aggregate measurement
Any candidates listed are tiered E3 or E4 and are not presented as targets ready to optimize

evals.name: attributes-layers-before-choosing-one
evals.prompt: /performance:target plugins/guard: the hook is a 125-line shell wrapper that execs a 1903-line Python guard body. The Python file is obviously where the time goes, so plan the optimization there.
evals.expected_output: Declines to select the Python body on size alone: line count is not a cost model. Requires cost attribution across the wrapper layer and the body layer before choosing either, naming a concrete per-layer measurement. Notes the shape of the known failure: in the source run the 125-line wrapper was roughly 88% of the cost and the 1903-line body was not the bottleneck.
expectations: Does not accept the 1903-line Python body as the target on file size alone
Requires cost attribution across the shell wrapper and the Python body before choosing a layer
States that line count is not a cost model
Names a concrete measurement that would attribute cost per layer

evals.name: anecdote-enters-the-list-at-e4-only
evals.prompt: /performance:target session: file edits felt really slow today, so put the edit path at the top of the ranking.
evals.expected_output: Admits the edit path onto the candidate list at E4 and no higher: session anecdote is a valid candidate source and an invalid ranking basis. Refuses to place it above any candidate carrying a measurement on the strength of the feeling, and names the drift-immune counter or instrument that would move it up the tiers.
expectations: Admits the edit path as a candidate at tier E4
Does not rank it above any measured candidate on the strength of the anecdote
States that session anecdote is a valid candidate source and an invalid ranking basis
Names the counter or instrument that would raise the candidate's tier

evals.name: names-the-counter-and-labels-the-generalization
evals.prompt: /performance:target the pre-tool hook chain: a census attributes 4 spawns per tool call to it. Give me the ranked table, and tell me why counting spawns beats timing them.
evals.expected_output: The ranked table names process spawns as the drift-immune counter that settles the candidate. Presents the counter as reproducible on a drifting host, never as more truthful than the duration, and labels counts-over-wall-clock for process spawns as this plugin's own generalization: the literature grounds it for instruction counts specifically, and Valgrind's own manual argues that execution time is what users perceive.
expectations: Names process spawns as the drift-immune counter for the candidate
Presents the counter as reproducible, never as more truthful than the duration
Labels counts-over-wall-clock for spawns as the plugin's own generalization, sourced only for instruction counts
Acknowledges the counter-argument that execution time is what users perceive
